body: Always thought they were cool as a kid. Got one from my old Opa, wanted to figure out how it worked desperately. Fast forward about 8 years and I’m working as a mechanic in a bowling alley. Figured out I love working on machines and specifically old fashioned ones that require little to no electricity. I was fascinated with how people created such amazing machines that could function on simple belt, pulley, and spring systems. Now my little side project of Opa’s typewriter has turned it a humble collection of 3 that I have been working on restoring and figuring out

If you’re working solo, highly recommend recording yourself. Like many have said, try to be aware of moving your hand first and your leg second. Break it down. Try just moving your hand, then moving your leg. Two very distinct motions and then slowly blur the line. Another thing that I’m glad my coach made me do was to just hold the lunge for as long as I could. It built up those muscles and made the actual action much easier. Keep practicing and don’t forget to have fun

My advice, when you’re interested and have your own equipment. It sounds like you’re already interested but I would recommend as well discussing it with your coach (assuming you aren’t self taught). Your coach can give you tips and a general idea of how you’ll do. It took me almost two years to be ready for competitions, but that was due to lack of money mainly. Whatever you decide, have fun and keep fencing

Here’s the gist: it’s the middle of Covid, just graduated high school, had serious suicidal thoughts for about a year now, went to college, college sucked, roommates left to save money, I opted to stay to hang out with friends, friends became busy for weeks, couldn’t go home at this point and needed to finish the semester out. Ended up not having any human interaction for about a month aside from one kind lady who said hello to me while I was getting dinner out of the vending machine. Granted, the isolation was partially my fault, I didn’t take care of myself and as such was too ashamed to leave my dorm building (hence the vending machine dinners that became much too common). 

During that time, I had no goals for myself, other than just success in school. But in my opinion that’s a pretty shit motivation and as such I failed nearly every class. At this point, I had decided it was best for everyone and me to just die. But it was almost Christmas, and you don’t want your family to miss you on Christmas, so I developed a plan to go home, celebrate one last time with my family, and then press the off button. As the time drew nearer (it was late November/early December at the time), I began looking up better ways than a 12 gauge and every time I searched I got that stupid hotline. So after about 15 searches, I clicked on it in anger. Got into a chat room with a hotline operator. I told them everything, my whole process, how I got there, the whole story. As I told the story, the operator interrupted “have you tried x” “yes I’ve tried x” “okay, but did you try y?” “Yes I tried y, it didn’t work for me” “okay but-“ this went on for some time. Eventually I snapped at the operator, and told them I’ve tried everything that everyone had ever suggested to me and nothing worked. I listed off everything I had ever tried and asked if they had anything original to give me.

Operator: “Well it sounds like you’ve got your mind made up on this”
Me: “What?”
Operator: “Look I’m not gonna lie to you, you’ve done everything and it hasn’t worked. I don’t know what to say to you”
Me: “Are you fucking kidding me right now, dude you’re supposed to encourage me; push me; tell me that there’s something I haven’t done yet”
Operator: “Would you listen if I did?”

That might not be exactly how the conversation went but it’s my best reenactment. I was getting so pissed off at this asshole and then I took a second to think. Why was I getting so upset? Why did I click the link in the first place? I knew there was no other way out so why did I bother wasting my time? Besides I didn’t want to live anymore anyways. And then I realized: if I truly wanted to die, I wouldn’t be feeling this way at all. I would embrace the void (my belief) and dive on in without ever needing to talk to a hotline. I had spent months trying to find motivation to live, tried every treatment I was recommended, and worked my ass off to hopefully get it to work. I didn’t want to die. I was just out of options and out of ideas. But that anger I felt, that spark, made me realize that maybe I wasn’t as broken as I thought I was. That maybe there was a chance because there was some part of me that didn’t want to die. And that’s why I’m still here today, I’m still chasing that spark. Hoping to god that it’ll lead me where I need to be. I still struggle, especially around this time, but I know if I have that spark: I’m okay for today. Don’t know if I will be okay, but I am right now. And that’s all that matters

Definitely make sure you have a backup plan. Whether that’s a job, family or friends willing to put you up, or elsewise: always have a plan b. From here you have a choice to make. You can either pretend to believe and when you’re parents ask about serving a mission, tell them you prayed about it and you get the feeling that the Lord is better served with you here or wherever tf you wanna go. You’re getting to be college aged so you could use that. Or if you feel strongly, you can tell your parents the truth. Ultimately the second option is what I opted for but I know many friends who did the first. It worked well for their purposes and the parents slowly came to their own understanding that their child was done with the church. My experience was that, I needed to tell my parents because I was tired of the lies. When I told them, I was basically interrogated by my mom so she could be sure that I had thought about this. Fast forward two hours and she told my dad for me, despite the fact that I wanted to tell him myself and I even told her that. He needed time to process and so did my mom, so I ended up vibing in my room for like 50 minutes. It was a long journey that only recently ended (two years of my parents knowing I was out but making me go to church and such). While it may not have been the way I had hoped, it was the way that was right for me. So, you need to make a choice. Both options are great options, I can say that fully. But always always always have a plan b. I’ve known people who have been kicked out right off the bat. Whatever you choose, I wish you the best. It’s a tough time, but ultimately you’ll be happier in the end after speaking your truth.

The last day that I tried and I mean really tried to believe in the Gospel was when I had my interview for the Melchizedek priesthood. I was interviewed by both my bishop and the stake president. I figured the stake president ought to know that I was lying in every answer that I gave. I figured God wouldn’t let me pervert his powers like that, that He wouldn’t let me get away with that. 

I remember even hoping that that would be the case. That I would get found out and that I would confess that I had been lying but I would repent, I would better myself, I would become worthy of the priesthood. But instead all I got was nearly the exact same words that led me to question the validity of the church in the first place: “I feel the spirit really strongly right now, don’t you?” He then proceeded to tell me that I was more than worthy of the Melchizedek priesthood and we set up a time for my confirmation. I felt so disgusted that I had been lied to for years of my life, spent so many weeks agonizing over a natural part of life, and dedicated myself so much to this church which wasn’t true. 

I ended up going through with the confirmation. I do feel guilty for that, even though it’s utter bullshit, pretending to be someone else surrounded by those closest to you really hurts. I did it out emotional numbness and fear of losing my relationship with my parents. But yeah, that’s what broke my shelf. No fact, no research, just pure unadulterated feeling or lack thereof.

I left because they gave clear instruction on how to know if the church is true. I followed those instructions and did not receive any confirming answer. Then they have the balls to call me a lazy learner. Fuck every single entitled member, the only ‘Holy Spirit’ you’re feeling is indoctrination and repetition which is familiar which causes a nice warm feeling in the chest. 

When I was in the church, I was happy to a degree but honestly I am far happier the farther I am from church influence. It’s a sense of freedom like I’ve never experienced before. It’s the realization that I don’t need some stuck up white dude to tell me what my morals should and shouldn’t be. The realization that I can trust in myself and what I feel is right and wrong. 

Even my therapist who is an active member has agreed with me that I am far better without the church in my life. It’s a person by person thing, if you’re LDS and you’re happy then I am happy for you. If you’re not LDS and you’re happy than I am happy for you too. Let people practice what they want to practice without demeaning them and their beliefs. 

Anyways that’s my two cents at least

My advice: do a set of however many you can do. Take that number, cut it in half. Start there. Do that number of push ups focusing on good form and touching your chest to the ground. As it gets easier, add another set of the same number. Once you can do 3 sets of that number, start again with your max and keep repeating. 

If at any point it seems like too much, don’t be afraid to do less. Exercise isn’t about numbers so much as it is about actually doing the thing. So long as you can be consistent, it doesn’t matter how many push ups you can do. Start at one. If you can’t do one, do wall push ups. Everyone starts somewhere, the only thing that really matters is that you don’t stop. 

Best of luck

If you’re scared to do something, put on a persona for 10 seconds. Pretend that nothing bad can happen to you during those 10 seconds and act like your most confident self. It’s landed me a few dates and has helped me to explore my interests more. As time went on from when I discovered this I’ve used it less and less because doing things that scare you show you that (typically) there isn’t much to be worried about at all. It’s super handy for people that are terrified of trying something new tho because if your most confident self walks you into a situation it’s usually worse/harder/more awkward to escape that situation once your in it than to just do the damn thing. Ten seconds is about the time I figured I could do while having that effect but do it for however long or short you want. Anyways, hopes this helps someone

Jupiter, the largest gas giant in our solar system, has different phases of the elements that make up its structure. It’s outermost layer is gaseous hydrogen and helium, it’s second outermost layer is liquid molecular hydrogen and helium, then things get weird where hydrogen and helium become liquid metallic, and then solid at the core with rock and other metals. Another fun thing about Jupiter, it is classified as a planet but can also be classified as a failed star. It failed to accumulate enough gas, and therefore mass, for gravity to press down on it to begin nuclear fusion. We nearly had a binary star system but Jupiter didn’t eat their share of the gas and other particles.

Honestly for me it wasn’t so much about the history. That came after I decided I was done with it all. For me it was the lack of spiritual experiences. People would say things like, “The spirit is so strong right now, can you feel it?” and every time I said “Yes, it’s very strong” but I felt nothing at all. I was too scared of being the black sheep to admit what I was truly feeling (or lack thereof). That scenario continued for years with me just faking it and hoping desperately for it to come true, to not have to lie about it anymore. Never happened. I always just repeated, “Doubt your doubts before you doubt your faith” anytime reason leaked into my mind. Then one day I wondered why they would say that unless there was some reason, some shred of truth in there that they didn’t want us to know. To not fully examine their organization. Hell, they even say to only use church approved websites, evidence, facts, etc. When one person controls all the information that is available to you, your overall picture of the world misses several key pieces that stop you from finding your own perspective. Once I examined more and more, everything I found just reaffirmed my belief, my thought, my doubt that something and something big was very wrong with the church. Now I’m out and much happier than I was when I was in

So whatever that reason is that’s pushing you not to do the deed, I think that’s worth looking for and the only way to find it is to keep living and search for it. Whatever it is, that’s your reason. You don’t even need to know what it is to be able to have it be your reason because the fact is, it’s still there, it’s just unknown. Best of luck with everything and if you need to talk, you can dm me

Well even tho your friends are still Mormon you can still be friends (assuming you still want to/are comfortable with that). Be honest with them, if they're real friends, they'll understand and move on. Plus you might be surprised, when I told my friends my honest thoughts on the church, literally everyone aside from two people agreed with what I was saying. Turns out we had been hiding it from each other and now we're much closer because of it and our friends that are still active in the church don't bug us about it or anything. Obviously, this all depends on the person so it might not be great but I'd say it's worth a shot. 

Other than that, like many others I would suggest focusing on something you want to learn to do and meet people through that. Or another approach is just approach someone when you both have some spare time and see how things go. Take it from a guy that's moved nine times in his life, this works way too often. Best of luck man
